record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether 3-CLIQUE, the problem of deciding whether an undirected simple loopless p-vertex graph contains a clique on three vertices, has the same algorithmic difficulty as Boolean matrix multiplication.

evidence.quote: Is 3-CLIQUE as difficult as Boolean matrix multiplication?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer. Boolean matrix multiplication (BMM) is the problem of computing, given two n×n matrices A, B with entries in {0,1}, the n×n matrix C with entries C[i,j] = OR over k of (A[i,k] AND B[k,j]). The 3-CLIQUE (triangle detection) problem is: given an undirected simple loopless graph on p vertices, decide whether it contains three pairwise adjacent vertices.

Say that two problems are "subcubically equivalent" if, for every ε > 0, a truly subcubic O(N^{3−ε}) time algorithm for one yields a truly subcubic algorithm for the other (with appropriate parameter identification p = Θ(n)).

Determine whether 3-CLIQUE has the same algorithmic difficulty as Boolean matrix multiplication. In particular, does there exist an algorithm solving 3-CLIQUE in time T(p) such that BMM on n×n Boolean matrices can be solved in time Õ(T(n))? Equivalently, can every improvement in the running time for triangle detection be transferred to an improvement for Boolean matrix multiplication?
artifact.status_search_result: Vassilevska Williams and Williams established a subcubic equivalence: an O(n^{3−ε}) algorithm for triangle detection would yield a truly subcubic algorithm for Boolean matrix multiplication, and vice versa. However, the stronger question of whether a triangle-detection algorithm running in time T(n) yields a BMM algorithm in time Õ(T(n)) (e.g., transferring polylogarithmic improvements) remains open, as does the broader question of exact equivalence in difficulty.

status_evidence.title: Subcubic Equivalences Between Path, Matrix, and Triangle Problems
status_evidence.snippet: BMM is subcubically equivalent to triangle detection: an O(n^{3−ε}) algorithm for one yields an O(n^{3−ε'}) algorithm for the other.
status_evidence.claim: The subcubic version of the equivalence between triangle detection and BMM is established.

status_evidence.title: An Improved Combinatorial Algorithm for Boolean Matrix Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: No O(n^{3−ε}) time combinatorial algorithms are known for BMM; relationship to triangle detection remains a central open question.
status_evidence.claim: The fine-grained relationship (beyond subcubic equivalence) is still open.
